name: Monoculturalism
summary: Monoculturalism holds that a state should rest on one shared national culture, language and set of values, which newcomers and minorities are expected to adopt rather than preserve alongside it. Its adherents argue that cultural diversity and group identities erode trust, cohesion and national identity, and so favour assimilation, a common language and limits on immigration. In its harshest forms it treats the dominant group's culture as superior and excludes or suppresses minorities.
scope: The mainstream assimilationist and cultural-nationalist strand as argued in Western debates since the 1990s: Samuel Huntington's defence of an Anglo-Protestant core, Schlesinger's critique of multicultural education, the German Leitkultur debate (Merz), and Merkel- and Cameron-style rejections of multiculturalism. It excludes racial-supremacist and ethnic-purity regimes, which the Wikipedia article also counts as monoculturalism, and the global-homogenisation sense of the term.

keyFigures.name: Samuel P. Huntington
keyFigures.role: Political scientist who argued that multiculturalism and weak assimilation threaten America's Anglo-Protestant national identity.

keyFigures.name: Arthur M. Schlesinger Jr.
keyFigures.role: Historian whose The Disuniting of America criticised multiculturalism as a threat to national unity.

keyFigures.name: Friedrich Merz
keyFigures.role: German CDU politician who in 2000 demanded immigrants assimilate to a German Leitkultur and proposed an annual immigration cap.

sources.usedFor: Defence of a single Anglo-Protestant core culture, English as the common language, assimilation, and opposition to bilingual education and group identities.

sources.usedFor: Scholarly statement of critics' positions on group rights, religious exemptions, national language and national identity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The sources discuss culture and integration, not health policy; adherents span Conservative, Christian Democrat and American conservative parties that differ on it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nothing in the monocultural case bears on wage floors, and proponents such as Merz, Cameron and Huntington do not share a line on it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Prominent proponents in the cited debate come from centre-right parties and lean pro-market, but this is inferred rather than part of the doctrine.

public-ownership.rationale: Centre-right proponents usually oppose broad nationalisation; this is inferred from their party affiliations, not from monocultural texts.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerns shared culture, and its proponents are split on taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no common adherent position on organized labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right politics of most proponents; nothing in the monocultural texts states a position on property rights.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed; proponents differ between market-liberal and economically interventionist nationalists.

cut-welfare.rationale: The doctrine does not address welfare levels (its welfare concern is who qualifies, see welfare-for-citizens), and proponents differ.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is foreign to the cultural-unity argument and to the centre-right parties of most proponents; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; security hawks and civil libertarians both appear among critics of multiculturalism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the cultural-conservative outlook of Huntington-style proponents that defend a traditional national culture; no source discusses drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Proponents such as Cameron stress free speech as a core national value; inferred, with the doctrine itself silent on speech law.

strong-leader.rationale: Not addressed; proponents work within parliamentary democracies and do not argue for bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Monoculturalism asks the state to uphold and transmit a common culture (Leitkultur tests, citizenship tests), so it rejects the view that the state is unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; American proponents lean against strict gun limits while European ones accept them.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; proponents differ on security spending.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the cultural-conservative lean of Huntington-style proponents; not discussed in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Neutral: the doctrine wants one national culture, which pulls toward national standards, but nothing says decisions must be centralised.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is outside the doctrine and its proponents split on it.

traditional-family.rationale: Huntington's Anglo-Protestant core includes traditional values, but the family is not a central claim of the doctrine.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; some proponents (Cameron) supported it while cultural conservatives oppose it, and Leitkultur debates cite liberal values on both sides.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; proponents are split along ordinary party lines.

more-religion-public.rationale: Huntington treats Christianity as part of the core culture, but Tibi and Leitkultur frame the core as secular Enlightenment values, so adherents are split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Huntington and Schlesinger blame group-identity politics for weakening national unity, so adherents resist race-conscious redress; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and proponents do not share a position.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending a single shared national culture against dilution is the core of the doctrine; Huntington calls Anglo-Protestant culture the bedrock of American identity and the Wikipedia article defines monoculturalism as preserving one culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Proponents defend inherited national culture and institutions, which fits gradualism, though the sources do not state it as a principle.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Merz proposed an annual cap of 200,000 on what German society could absorb and Scheffer spoke of exhausted absorptive capacity, though others in the camp only demand better integration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Huntington's concern for national identity implies scepticism of supranational authority; inferred, not stated in the sources.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; proponents split between free-traders and protectionists.

nation-first.rationale: A doctrine centred on one national culture tends to prioritise national interests, but the sources address culture rather than foreign policy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents differ.

open-borders.rationale: A doctrine that worries that scale and speed of immigration prevent assimilation (Huntington, Scheffer) rejects open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; proponents are divided.

revolution-justified.rationale: Proponents are defenders of existing national institutions and work within parliaments; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right politics of the main proponents; nothing in the sources discusses planning.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism and free trade both appear among proponents of cultural unity, so no common answer.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing money would break with the established national order that monoculturalism defends, and no proponent proposes it; inferred from conservative stance.

one-party-rule.rationale: Proponents argue within liberal democracies (Merkel, Cameron, Schlesinger), so a single guiding party is not part of their case.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; monarchy fits some national traditions but the doctrine does not take sides.

democracy-best.rationale: Huntington, Schlesinger and Cameron argue for national unity within democratic states, and Cameron's defence of democracy and the rule of law is among the core values listed.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power are alien to the national-culture case; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Huntington fears the nation dividing into two peoples, so a regional right to leave is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Proponents appeal to a shared culture, not to a natural governing class; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mainstream proponents work through elections and law; the stance is inferred rather than documented.

separate-church-state.rationale: Leitkultur defenders (Tibi) stress secularism while Huntington counts Christianity as part of the core culture, so adherents split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Leitkultur and Cameron's muscular liberalism ground the national culture in secular law, democracy and rights, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The doctrine relies on the state to transmit and enforce national norms; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Wikipedia article ties monoculturalism to one social or ethnic group's culture, but Huntington's mainstream version defines the core by culture and creed, not descent.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Huntington sees culture and identity as drivers of history, not class conflict; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Group-based equalisation is the kind of identity politics these critics blame for disunity; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Special group authority within the state conflicts with a single common national culture and law; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Huntington's civilizational thinking points that way, but the doctrine concerns one state's culture, so adherents are split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Leitkultur stresses shared obligations to national values, but proponents also insist on individual rights as core values, so they split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The doctrine does not criticise industrial society and proponents are mainstream conservatives; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Emphasis on continuity of inherited culture makes disruptive acceleration unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Defenders of the existing national culture sometimes invoke a lost cohesion (Huntington on older assimilation), but the doctrine is not essentially restorationist.

direct-action.rationale: Proponents use parliamentary and legal channels; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A hunter-gatherer return would dissolve the national culture the doctrine aims to preserve and no proponent suggests it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Alien to the doctrine and to its centre-right proponents; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right politics of the main proponents; not discussed in the sources.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right politics of the main proponents; not discussed in the sources.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory is foreign to the doctrine; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The doctrine is nationalist-cultural and operates within liberal democracies; class dictatorship is incompatible with it.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from the conservative stance; not addressed by the sources.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory of imperialism is not part of the doctrine; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Proponents rely on state-run citizenship and integration programmes, so they accept taxation; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Leitkultur and Cameron want the state to promote shared values actively (muscular liberalism), which strains a pure harm principle, but they also defend liberal rights.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Critics of multiculturalism such as Kukathas and Barry deny group rights, but the cultural-unity case also asks citizens to uphold a collective culture, so only a mild lean.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the doctrine's focus on belonging to one national community.

state-as-business.rationale: The doctrine treats the nation as a cultural community, not a customer relationship; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Huntington and Schlesinger blame academic and elite promotion of multiculturalism for weakening national identity, which echoes this claim, though they do not say it is the main power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Huntington's mainstream version explains difference by culture, not heredity; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Leitkultur proponents want shared values, not state direction of every area of life; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Huntington warns of decline in national identity, but the doctrine does not call for radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The doctrine concerns preserving one culture within a state; expansion would add diversity; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: No proponent defends serfdom and it conflicts with the liberal-democratic framework of the mainstream strand.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Schlesinger and Huntington criticise relativist multiculturalists who treat Western heritage as merely another power-laden tradition.

universal-morality.rationale: Tibi grounds Leitkultur in universal Enlightenment values while Huntington stresses a particular culture, so adherents split.

single-common-good.rationale: A single shared culture and creed as the basis of unity fits this, though the sources do not discuss it as political theory.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine wants the existing common language kept central, but revival is outside its scope.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the centre-right politics of the main proponents; not discussed.

national-self-determination.rationale: A doctrine of one national culture sits naturally with nations governing themselves, but the sources address culture, not a right of nations to statehood.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Tibi's Leitkultur draws on Enlightenment reason while Huntington counts Protestant Christianity as part of the core, so adherents split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Proponents link national solidarity to a shared identity (Barry, Gitlin on cohesion), which supports reserving benefits, though this is not a central claim.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inherited cultural institutions carry the national culture the doctrine exists to preserve, so sacrificing them for new creation is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from a Western-centric outlook such as Huntington's.

workers-nation.rationale: The doctrine puts national cultural unity above class organisation but does not discuss labour organising; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Huntington-style conservatives may favour traditional roles, but Cameron's muscular liberalism defends women's rights, so adherents split.

ban-interest.rationale: Alien to the Western national cultures proponents defend; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The mainstream strand defines belonging by culture and creed and offers assimilation, not racial classification; Merkel, Cameron and Huntington all work within equal citizenship.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist state theory is foreign to the doctrine; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Huntington blames weak assimilation for the problem, Merz demanded that immigrants adopt Germany's core cultural values, and Merkel urged integration into German culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Huntington's argument is about slow assimilation and policy neglect, not a deliberate plot; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Huntington treats American creed as national identity but the doctrine concerns domestic culture, not spreading it abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from the conservative stance; not addressed by the sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Huntington criticises elite indifference to national identity but does not call elites corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not part of the mainstream strand and is incompatible with the liberal-democratic framing of its proponents.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Leitkultur and citizenship tests ask the state to promote a common culture, which exceeds a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Huntington stresses that assimilation includes intermarriage, so discouraging mixing runs against the mainstream account.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The mainstream strand grounds national belonging in a creed of equal rights and offers assimilation to all; the Wikipedia article notes the ethnocentric form that does not.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist theory is foreign to the doctrine; inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Huntington frames the Anglo-Protestant settler culture as the founding bedrock of the US, not as a colonial project.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Leitkultur and the assimilationist case want one common set of national norms and law, without parallel legal communities.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Leitkultur defenders ground the national culture in secular liberal values including freedom of worship; Cameron lists freedom of worship among them.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Huntington values Christian heritage while Leitkultur defenders favour secular schooling, so adherents split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Proponents work within liberal democracies and cite democracy as a core value; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: The Wikipedia article lists suppression and exclusion as forms of monoculturalism, but the mainstream proponents propose assimilation and immigration limits rather than expulsion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Huntington's clash-of-civilizations work stresses rivalry among peoples, but the doctrine does not state it as a driver of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Defenders of a muscular defence of national values, as in German constitutional practice, accept limits on anti-constitutional parties; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Rule of law and constitutional order are among values proponents such as Cameron name; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: A vanguard party of revolutionaries is incompatible with the doctrine and with its democratic proponents.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Huntington warns of two peoples, cultures and languages, and Putnam and Blainey are cited for the claim that diversity erodes trust and cohesion; this is the central premise of the doctrine.

party-controls-media.rationale: Proponents defend free speech as a core national value (Cameron); inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Alien to the liberal-democratic framing of mainstream proponents.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship tests and integration requirements (Australia, German states) imply a demanding path to citizenship, though length of residence is not specifically argued.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Lammert and Huntington root identity in a particular culture and nation, which weighs against pooling sovereignty, though Lammert reframes at the European level.

clerical-rule.rationale: Leitkultur and muscular liberalism root authority in secular democracy and law, so rule by religious scholars is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Doctrine of national cultural loyalty implies supporting one's country in war; revolutionary defeatism is incompatible.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Huntington favours Western alliance cohesion on civilizational grounds; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Huntington and Schlesinger fault academic and elite promotion of multiculturalism for ignoring national feeling, but do not make the general claim.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Wikipedia article says monoculturalism rests on the belief that the dominant group's practices are superior, and Cliteur and Huntington hold Western culture and law superior to some alternatives.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Huntington values Protestant heritage but does not address school curricula.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The ethnic form of monoculturalism implies descent, but the civic assimilationist form accepts newcomers who adopt the culture, so adherents split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Huntington explicitly opposes bilingual education and dual-language programmes as threats to a single common language of the nation.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Critics of multiculturalism such as Barry reject special accommodations for religion, and Leitkultur requires one common set of norms.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Emphasis on conformity to a common culture; inferred rather than stated.

collective-defense.rationale: Huntington values Western allied cohesion, though not directly discussed in the cited essay; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Leitkultur defenders favour secular supremacy while Huntington defends Christianity's cultural role, so adherents split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Fear of the nation splitting into two peoples suggests support for keeping the state together, though force is not discussed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Different legal and cultural systems within one state conflict with the single-culture ideal; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Alien to the liberal-democratic framing of its proponents.

character-from-environment.rationale: Assimilation policy presumes that upbringing and culture shape people, as Huntington says of third- and fourth-generation immigrants; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule of law is among the values Leitkultur and Cameron's speech name as core.

leader-cult.rationale: Alien to the liberal-democratic framing of proponents; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist theory foreign to the doctrine.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The mainstream strand is about a state's own culture within its borders, not claims on co-nationals abroad; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Leitkultur defenders and Cameron list freedom of worship among core values.

women-must-cover.rationale: Cameron's muscular liberalism and Leitkultur stress women's rights and secular norms, and are directed against practices seen as incompatible with national values.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Critics of multiculturalism object that separate self-governing minority institutions and enclaves undermine a shared identity, and Huntington opposes separate enclaves.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Assimilationists urge minorities to integrate where they live; the question of founding a separate homeland is not addressed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Huntington attributes outcomes to culture, so he rejects materialist explanation; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; proponents defend the rule of law and majoritarian national identity at once.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Group-based representation sits against the colour-blind civic stance critics take; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Alien to the doctrine and its parliamentary proponents.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Huntington and Schlesinger criticise multicultural education for reducing Western heritage to crimes, and the doctrine wants school history built around the national tradition.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Cliteur and Huntington hold Western culture superior, but they do not argue for rule over other societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: Schools transmitting loyalty to a common national culture are central to the assimilationist case against multicultural education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Huntington blames race-based group identities for weakening national identity, which points to opposing racial preferences, but he does not discuss admissions.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; proponents come from market-integrated Western states.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist theory foreign to the doctrine.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Proponents defend equal citizenship, but libertarian-leaning adherents might accept it; weakly inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Veto by dissenters would block the common national norms the doctrine wants enforced; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, except that Stoffman objects to dog meat as incompatible with Canadian culture.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The doctrine is an explicitly political project about national identity; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory foreign to the doctrine; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Ethnic forms of monoculturalism might favour it but the civic assimilationist form does not, so adherents split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Group-based political leadership by descent conflicts with a single common national culture and civic equality; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream proponents such as Schlesinger and Huntington accept mainstream historiography.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Defence of inherited national heritage against Western heritage being reduced to crimes (Schlesinger) points to keeping the monuments.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Huntington holds that American institutions derive from a particular Anglo-Protestant culture, and Cliteur treats Western institutions as culturally specific.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Proponents defend civilian democratic institutions; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary government is the setting of the mainstream strand; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Huntington says immigrants can share the American dream only in English and opposes bilingual programmes, and critics cite language tests as policy.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Race-conscious remedies reinforce the group identities Huntington blames for disunity; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, though Cameron pledged to withhold state funding from groups that discourage integration.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Huntington raises fertility differences as a concern, which fits seeing demographic policy as an alternative to immigration; not stated as a remedy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Proponents emphasise rule of law; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The mainstream strand argues from non-assimilation, not from secret plotting; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the cultural-conservative stance; not addressed by the sources.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Priority of national cultural self-definition over outside authority is implied, but not discussed explicitly in the sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Huntington stresses Protestant culture but defines identity by culture and creed, while Leitkultur defenders define it secularly, so adherents split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Huntington counts Christianity as part of the national core, so adherents reject treating religion as illusion; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist feminist claim foreign to the doctrine.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Defending a national language is in the spirit of the doctrine, but loanword purism is not addressed.

majority-settlement.rationale: Ethnic forms of monoculturalism could back it but mainstream proponents argue for assimilation, so adherents split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mainstream proponents appeal to liberal-democratic Western values; denial is outside the doctrine.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Cameron and Leitkultur defenders cite liberal values among the core; cultural conservatives might differ.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Proponents defend democracy and free speech as core values.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Leitkultur and Cameron's muscular liberalism list freedom of speech and worship as national values.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine concerns domestic culture.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Rejected by Leitkultur and muscular liberalism, which defend secular constitutional government.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Huntington and Schlesinger criticise identity-group politics; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist concept foreign to the doctrine.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Cliteur argues Western culture and law are superior to some non-Western practices and Merz and Scheffer targeted failed integration, but Tibi and Cameron separate Islam from extremism, so it is a lean only.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Leitkultur and muscular liberalism ground authority in secular democracy and law.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Quebec's Bill 21 and French-style laïcité fit single-culture views while Anglo-American proponents oppose such bans, so adherents split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: A doctrine of defending one national community would not endorse disarmament; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Proponents accept universal citizenship under shared culture; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claim foreign to the doctrine.

reification.rationale: Marxist concept foreign to the doctrine.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marxist critique foreign to the doctrine.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law is among the values Leitkultur and Cameron's speech name as core; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The mainstream strand offers assimilation and citizenship on cultural terms, and Merkel, Cameron and Huntington all work within a universal franchise.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Huntington treats intermarriage as a sign of assimilation, so restricting it opposes the mainstream strand.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Mainstream proponents argue for integration, not exclusion of minorities; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Huntington counts Christianity as part of the national core and Leitkultur defenders favour secular neutrality, not state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Alien to the doctrine and its law-and-order centre-right proponents.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Huntington opposes institutionalised communal division; consociational power-sharing between communities contradicts the single-culture ideal.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources concern culture and integration, not poverty relief; adherents among conservatives lean to charity while Christian Democrats back the welfare state.

term-limits.rationale: Nothing in the monocultural case bears on term limits, and proponents such as Merz, Cameron and Huntington do not share a line on it.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on a single national political community and its institutions; the sources do not discuss delegable voting, which most adherents would see as an unfamiliar departure.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources never touch extinction risk, and adherents have no shared position on it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The sources discuss a shared culture, not church governance; adherents run from Christian conservatives who oppose it to secular ones who accept it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the Leitkultur and Huntington arguments that newcomers should accept core liberal values, which include equality between spouses; the sources do not state this as a position on marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: assimilationists tie full political membership to adopting the common culture, which points to naturalisation before voting; the sources do not discuss local suffrage.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is outside the sources; adherents across conservative parties split on rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: mainstream cultural-nationalist conservatives defend property rights; the sources never address intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the Western assimilationist strand argues for shared culture through schools and civic norms, not drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the strand's mainstream conservative, security-minded politics; the sources do not discuss nuclear basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Adherents are split between Atlanticist conservatives and sovereignty-minded nationalists; the sources are silent.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split on formal genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Economic distribution is not part of the definition, and adherents range across market and welfare views.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the strand's conservative mainstream accepts defensive force; the sources do not discuss pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from Huntington's picture of an enduring Anglo-Protestant core that newcomers are expected to join.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: culturally conservative adherents generally resist constructivist accounts of sex; not discussed in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the strand opposes group-identity politics, which extends to identity categories within feminism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; honouring the nation's dead is common among adherents but not a defining position.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: the strand is civic-cultural rather than apocalyptic or religious in its politics.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; the strand focuses on cohesion inside the state, not on diaspora relations.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from Leitkultur and Huntington, who treat a shared culture as the basis of the state and of citizenship.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between religious conservatives and secular assimilationists.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: culturally traditional adherents are unlikely to adopt a feminist test of religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: the strand asks minorities to adopt the common culture and join the economy, not to be excluded from it; its harsher forms are out of scope.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: the strand stresses one state-wide common culture, not carving up regions for separate peoples.

independent-unions.rationale: The sources discuss culture and integration, not labour; adherents differ.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not a monocultural issue; adherents span left and right.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not a monocultural issue; adherents differ on public ownership.

second-chamber.rationale: Not a monocultural issue; adherents differ on legislative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on a single national culture and state, not community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the stress on one national culture and common rules over local self-rule.

family-wage.rationale: Not a monocultural issue; adherents differ.

person-over-state.rationale: Adherents emphasise shared national values over individual preference, but the mainstream strand also upholds individual rights; split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Huntington defends an Anglo-Protestant core with religion as part of national identity; inferred for spirituality.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on one national legal and cultural order, which favours central authority over regional distinctiveness.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The mainstream strand in scope defends a shared national culture, not racial groups, and excludes racial-supremacist regimes.

racial-pride.rationale: The mainstream strand speaks of national culture, not race; adherents split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Adherents stress a shared language as the core of a state's culture, but their nation is bounded by the state, so the statement's cross-border claim splits them.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from its demand for one common civic culture, which opposes separate group-based political representation (s3).

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Adherents warn of internal fragmentation (s1) more than of foreign plots, and are split on external ones.

free-public-college.rationale: The ideology is about culture and assimilation and does not take a stand on tuition; adherents are split by general economic views.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; adherents divide along ordinary left-right lines on environmental policy.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on handing on a national heritage and identity to later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of group-specific identities and viewpoints in public life (s3).

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on national strength and security, though the sources do not discuss arms.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between market and protectionist views.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the position favours a strong common state and rule of law, which implies this, so it is inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Defenders of a national core culture generally stress loyalty and military service to the nation; never discussed, so inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; the position is about culture and identity, and adherents are split on labour policy.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; the position is about culture and identity, and adherents are split on welfare policy.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from fiscal conservatives to state-minded nationalists.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The position puts national interest and the national core first and is wary of global redistribution; never discussed, so inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Adherents work within existing parliamentary states and defend their institutions; revolutionary replacement of the state is far from the position.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The position wants one shared national culture and set of values rather than a free variety of ways of living; inferred as it is not about economics.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split on environmental policy.

sacred-nation.rationale: Huntington and the Leitkultur debate ground national identity in a shared culture and creed that outlasts individuals, though most arguments are civic and cultural rather than sacral.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split on higher-education policy.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The position treats the nation as a unified cultural community and rejects group-based grievance claims, so regional-exploitation claims sit poorly with it; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Conservative defenders of a national core culture often appeal to universal human nature and dignity as the shared base; never discussed directly, so inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between valuing national broadcasters as carriers of common culture and distrusting them.

religions-one-truth.rationale: A defence of one national core culture, as in Huntington's Anglo-Protestant core, does not accept all religions as equally true; the sources do not discuss it.

farm-price-support.rationale: The sources cover culture and integration, not farm policy; adherents range across parties that differ on farm subsidies.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the national-security conservatism of most adherents, who prefer a deterrent while rivals keep theirs.

workers-own-party.rationale: Monoculturalists stress one shared national community over group and class identities; inferred, as the sources say nothing on workers' parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Critics of multiculturalism say group customs cannot override national law, and the sources note religious exemptions as a dispute; not stated about FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Leitkultur debate names secular core values such as equality as what newcomers must accept, which includes equal property rights for women.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A single national language is central; inferred that varieties are treated as one language, though the sources do not address naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The sources do not discuss environmental law, and adherents across conservative parties split on courts versus agencies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: A common national culture and law applies to all, so a separate formal role for customary chiefs is unlikely; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the mainstream conservative stress on liberty, so adherents would resist overriding it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the law-and-order conservatism of most adherents.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Huntington argues English must be the common language and opposes bilingual education, and Merz's Leitkultur demands newcomers assimilate.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The sources deal with culture and integration, not labour law, and adherents across conservative parties differ on union membership.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the stress on citizenship and a shared civic identity, which suits proof of citizenship at the ballot; the sources do not address voter ID.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Leitkultur and Anglo-Protestant core arguments, which give the host culture's religious tradition a leading place; no source addresses legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The sources concern culture and integration rather than the definition of democracy, so adherents have no common line.

premarital-sex.rationale: Adherents range from religious conservatives to secular liberals and the sources do not address sexual morality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Nothing in the monocultural case bears on internet shutdowns, and adherents do not share a line on it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is outside the monocultural case and its proponents differ across parties.

women-suffrage.rationale: Mainstream adherents accept women's equal political rights, and Leitkultur versions list sexual equality among the secular core values.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Leitkultur critics often cite Islam on women's status while Christian conservative adherents reject the claim, so adherents are split.

race-social-construct.rationale: The mainstream strand argues from culture, not biology, and treats racial-supremacist doctrine as outside its scope; its sources do not discuss the concept.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The sources do not address gender-equality policy and adherents differ on it.

missingStatements.text: Immigrants and their children should adopt the country's common language and way of life rather than keep separate communities.
missingStatements.rationale: Huntington and Merz both frame the problem as enclaves and failed assimilation and ask newcomers to take on the core culture.

missingStatements.text: Schools should not teach the history and values of minority cultures as separate subjects alongside the national culture.
missingStatements.rationale: Schlesinger and Huntington attack multicultural education and group-identity curricula as weakening common national identity.

missingStatements.text: Applicants for citizenship should have to pass a test of the national language, history and values.
missingStatements.rationale: Citizenship tests (Australia from 2007, German state tests) are the policy instruments the assimilationist critics of multiculturalism endorse.
missingStatements.declined: Citizenship tests are a narrow policy instrument; long-naturalization-wait and assimilate-immigrants cover the position.

notes: The doctrine is thin on economics, foreign policy and most social questions, so many answers are low-confidence inferences from the mainly centre-right politics of its proponents. A civic form (Huntington, Tibi, Cameron) and an ethnic form (as described in the Wikipedia article) differ on ethnic-nation, citizenship-by-descent and exclusion; the profile follows the civic form.
